blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Agents today often take real world actions which depend on long term memory and context recall over time. However, most current memory benchmarks are built for a conversational question-answer format, where the question itself signals that some fact must be retrieved, and often which one. Moreover, benchmarks rarely require anything beyond accuracy from submissions, allowing memory systems to make unreasonable cost/time tradeoffs to achieve higher scores. We present DolphinBench, a benchmark that evaluates memory directly through an agent’s task completion. DolphinBench includes three knowledge-work personas with roughly 500k tokens of user messages per persona and evaluates agents on tasks which depend on information from that history. We verify all 200 tasks per persona by running an agent with and without the relevant history, requiring success with it and failure without it. Finally, we require all evaluations to report total cost and latency alongside accuracy, which enables us to evaluate agent memory systems holistically. No existing memory benchmark combines all three. The dataset and evaluation code are available at https://dolphinbench.ai .
blocks.zh: 今天的代理人往往采取现实世界的行动,这些行动取决于长期记忆和背景的回顾。 然而,目前大多数的内存基准都是为对话式的问答格式而构建的,其中问题本身表示某些事实必须检索,而且常常是哪个事实. 此外,基准很少从提交材料中需要超出准确性的任何内容,使内存系统能够作出不合理的成本/时间权衡,以达到更高的分数。 Dolphin Bench是直接通过代理任务完成来评估记忆的基准。 Dolphin Bench包括三个知识-工作人物,每人有大约500k的用户信息信使,并评价代理商的工作取决于该历史的信息。 我们通过管理一个有相关历史和没有相关历史的代理人来核实每个人的所有200项任务,这需要成功和失败。 最后,我们要求所有评价报告总成本和耐久性,同时报告准确性,使我们能够对代理记忆系统进行整体评价。 没有现有的内存基准将全部三者合并. 数据集和评价代码见https://dolphinbench.ai。 。 。 。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: The world is rapidly adopting agents in real world tasks, from software engineering [ 8 ] and web tasks [ 31 ] to customer service [ 28 ] and long running projects [ 26 ] . Such agents are increasingly required to keep track of information across project histories and past sessions that outgrow their context windows, which memory systems [ 16 , 4 , 20 ] are built to manage. It is important to evaluate this capability with memory benchmarks.
blocks.zh: 世界正在迅速在现实世界的任务中采用代理,从软件工程[8]和网络任务[31]到客户服务[28]和长期运行的项目[26]. 越来越多地要求这些代理人跟踪项目历史和过去会议中的信息,这些历史和会议超越了上下文窗口,而内存系统[16、4、20]是用来管理的。 必须用记忆基准评估这种能力。

blocks.en: Memory benchmarks have largely not adapted to this setting. The dominant evaluation format is question answering [ 30 , 14 , 27 ] , where a system ingests a long history and answers questions about it. Such evaluations are inherently biased though, as a direct question acts as a signal to the system that some fact must be retrieved, and frequently mentions which fact. A QA benchmark asks “What messaging platform does the team use?”, which already announces that a platform fact exists and is wanted; an action-based test of the same fact instead instructs the agent to post an update in the team’s channel, and never mentions platforms at all. So, the evaluation effectively begins only after the most difficult step, recognizing that retrieval is required at all, has been completed on the system’s behalf. An agent acting under an instruction may get a weaker hint, but nothing in the format guarantees one. Evaluating memory for agents requires removing the question and using memory-dependent tasks as the accuracy signal.
blocks.zh: 记忆基准基本上没有适应这种设置。 最主要的评价格式是回答问题[30,14,27],其中一个系统吸收了很长的历史,并回答了与此有关的问题. 然而,这种评价本质上是有偏见的,因为直接的问题向系统表明,必须检索某些事实,并经常提到哪个事实。 一个QA基准询问“团队使用什么信息平台? ” , 已经宣布平台事实存在, 并被通缉; 基于同一事实的行动测试却指示代理在团队频道上发布更新, 因此,只有在认识到完全需要检索的最困难步骤才代表系统有效地开始评价。 根据指示行事的代理人可能会得到较弱的暗示,但格式中没有任何保证. 评价代理机的内存需要删除问题,并以内存依赖的任务作为准确信号.

blocks.en: Memory benchmarks commonly run into two further limitations, the first of which is in the range of metrics demanded from a valid solution. Since memory and information retrieval is an optimization problem where tradeoffs can be chosen, a full evaluation requires comparing accuracy, cost, and latency. A system can achieve high accuracy, for instance, by re-reading the entire history at each query with frontier models, incurring significant latency and compute costs that a production deployment could not sustain. We therefore require every result to report total cost and median task latency alongside accuracy.
blocks.zh: 记忆基准通常还存在另外两个局限性,第一个局限在有效解决方案要求的计量范围内。 由于内存和信息检索是一个可以选择权衡的优化问题,因此全面评价需要比较准确性,成本和耐久性. 例如,一个系统可以实现高精度,方法是在每次查询时都用前沿模型重新阅读整个历史,产生相当大的耐久性和计算成本,而生产部署是无法维持的。 因此,我们要求每个结果都报告总费用和中位数任务延迟以及准确性。

blocks.en: Second, because most benchmarks are generated synthetically and at scale, they are prone to defects: incorrect answer keys, mislabeled supporting evidence, and questions that are unanswerable even given the complete history [ 17 , 12 ] . Most benchmarks do not establish that each of their tests is actually solvable by a capable agent with perfect memory, which imposes an unknown ceiling on every reported score in case of such defects. We therefore verify every DolphinBench test using an agent with oracle memory: we provide the relevant history and require the agent to complete the task, then withhold that history and require it to fail. This checks that the task can be completed and that withholding the history affects success.
blocks.zh: 第二,由于大多数基准是合成和规模生成的,因此容易出现缺陷:答案键不正确,贴错标签的佐证证据,以及即使考虑到完整的历史[17,12]也无法回答的问题. 大多数基准没有确定,他们的每一项试验实际上都可以由具有完美记忆的能干剂溶解,在出现这种缺陷时,对每一次报告的分数规定了一个未知的上限。 因此,我们用一个具有甲骨文记忆的特工来验证每一次海豚奔驰测试:我们提供相关的历史,并要求特工完成任务,然后扣下这个历史,要求它失败. 这样做可以检查任务能否完成,而隐瞒历史会影响成功。

blocks.en: We introduce DolphinBench, a benchmark that evaluates agent memory through real world simulated actions. DolphinBench defines three knowledge-work personas: a startup CEO, an infrastructure engineer, and a product manager. We then simulate years of conversation (user input and tasks) for each persona with their agent. An agent processes this history and is then issued tasks whose correct actions depend on specific pieces of information within the session history.
blocks.zh: 我们引入了海豚奔驰(Dolphin Bench),这个基准通过真实世界模拟动作来评价代理记忆. Dolphin Bench定义了三个知识-工作人物:一个启动的首席执行官,一个基础设施工程师,以及一个产品经理. 然后我们模拟每个人与他们的代理人交谈的年代(用户输入和任务)。 一个代理处理这个历史,然后被发布任务,其正确行动取决于会话历史中的具体信息.

blocks.en: Together, these choices give DolphinBench three properties that existing memory benchmarks do not combine: tests that evaluate memory through action rather than recall, results that report cost and latency alongside accuracy, and verification of every test through agent runs with and without the relevant history. Across the evaluated models and harnesses, the highest-scoring agent completes 70.67% of tasks. The memory systems rank differently across agents, and the most expensive agent is neither the most accurate nor the fastest.
blocks.zh: 这些选择加在一起,赋予了海豚奔驰三种特性,现有的内存基准并没有结合:通过动作而不是回忆来评价内存的测试,报告成本和耐久性以及准确性的结果,通过代理运行和没有相关历史来验证每一个测试. 在整个被评价的模型和工具中,评分最高的代理完成70.67%的任务. 内存系统在不同代理商之间的排名不同,最昂贵的代理商既不是最准确的,也不是最快的.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: We identify three properties that are important for a memory benchmark for agents which mitigate the key issues faced by such benchmarks in practice. • The test format must require action rather than pure text responses in a question-answer format. • The final evaluation results must include cost and latency alongside accuracy. • Each test should be solvable by the agent once it has perfect memory, and unsolvable without it (i.e. no ground truth errors, no hidden assumptions, and no tests that pass regardless of memory).
blocks.zh: 我们查明了三种特性,这些特性对于减轻这些基准在实践中面临的关键问题的代理人的记忆基准很重要。 测试格式必须要求行动,而不是以回答问题的形式提供纯文本的答复。 最后的评价结果必须包括费用和耐久性以及准确性。 • 支助 每个测试一旦拥有完美的内存,就应该被代理者溶解,没有它就无法溶解(即没有地面的真伪错误,没有隐藏的假设,没有通过无论内存的测试).

blocks.en: The test format must require action rather than pure text responses in a question-answer format.
blocks.zh: 测试格式必须要求行动,而不是以问答格式的纯文本回答.

blocks.en: The final evaluation results must include cost and latency alongside accuracy.
blocks.zh: 最后的评价结果必须包括费用和耐久性以及准确性。

blocks.en: Each test should be solvable by the agent once it has perfect memory, and unsolvable without it (i.e. no ground truth errors, no hidden assumptions, and no tests that pass regardless of memory).
blocks.zh: 每个测试一旦拥有完美的内存,就应该被代理者溶解,没有它就无法溶解(即没有地面的真伪错误,没有隐藏的假设,没有通过无论内存的测试).

blocks.en: Table 1 shows how prior memory benchmarks compare to DolphinBench on each property. The following subsections develop on the justification and existing work for each principle in turn.
blocks.zh: 表1显示之前的内存基准在每个属性上如何与海豚奔驰相比. 以下各小节分别阐述每项原则的理由和现有工作。

blocks.en: Table 1: Memory benchmarks compared on the three properties an action-based memory evaluation requires. ✓ : yes, ✗ : no, ∼ \sim : partial: a latency but no cost; b latency only in an appendix; c token counts as the only cost signal, no latency; d actions in a story/text-game setting rather than app state; e checks task design and information disclosure after evaluation; f timing and token counts, but no monetary cost; g monetary cost but no latency.
blocks.zh: 表1:基于动作的内存评价需要比较三个属性的内存基准。 a 耐久但无费用;b 耐久只存在于附录中;c 象征值计为唯一成本信号,无耐久性;d 在一个故事/文字游戏设定中的行动,而不是应用状态;e 检查任务设计和评价后的信息披露;f 计时和象征值,但没有货币成本;g 货币成本,但没有耐久性。

blocks.en: 2.1 Task Format
blocks.zh: 2.1 任务格式

blocks.en: Memory evaluation began as conversational QA [ 30 , 14 ] , later expanding into categories like temporal reasoning, knowledge updates, and abstention [ 27 , 7 ] while keeping the QA format. The format carries the retrieval signal discussed in the introduction, and an action-style task removes it: the agent has to “know to remember”, which makes such tasks both harder and more representative of real world usage.
blocks.zh: 记忆评价开始于对话QA[30,14],后来扩展为时间推理,知识更新等类别,并在保留QA格式的同时弃权. 格式带有导言中讨论的检索信号,一种动作式的任务消除了它:代理人必须“知道要记住”,这使这种任务更加困难,更能代表真实世界的使用。

blocks.en: Some recent benchmarks have moved toward action-based testing. Mem2ActBench [ 21 ] scores agents on task completion in simulated environments; MemoryArena [ 6 ] evaluates interdependent agentic subtasks; STATE-Bench [ 11 ] tests stateful agent actions; MEMTRACK [ 5 ] tracks state across interleaved Slack, Linear, and Git timelines.
blocks.zh: 最近的一些基准已转向基于行动的测试。 Mem2 Act Bench [21] 在模拟环境下完成任务时给代理记分; MemoryArena [6] 评价相互依存的代理子任务; STATE-Bench [11] 测试状态代理动作; MEMTRACK [5] 轨迹状态跨越间断的Slack, Linear, 和 Git 时间表.

blocks.en: 2.2 Metrics
blocks.zh: 2.2 计量

blocks.en: Most benchmarks do not require cost and latency, making the partial reporting on these benchmarks inconsistent. For example, STATE-Bench reports dollar cost per task but not latency; MemoryArena reports latency but no aggregate cost; MemoryAgentBench reports memory construction and query execution times but not monetary cost. However, neither cost nor latency alone is enough, since inference choices like batch size and hardware trade them off. Thus, both these metrics should appear in any valid submission.
blocks.zh: 大多数基准并不要求费用和耐久性,使关于这些基准的部分报告不一致。 例如,STATE-Bench报告每个任务花费1美元,但不能长期存在; MemoryArena报告延迟,但没有总成本; MemoryAgent Bench报告内存构建和查询执行时间,但不报告货币成本. 然而,光靠成本或耐久性都是不够的,因为像批量大小和硬件这样的推论选择可以将它们交换。 因此,这两个衡量标准都应出现在任何有效的提交材料中。

blocks.en: Accuracy alone is also easy to skew: the same benchmark can produce very different numbers under a modified judge prompt or judge model, with Penfield Labs [17] showing that one evaluated judge configuration accepted approximately 63% of deliberately incorrect, topically related answers. Cost and latency are harder to quietly improve, which makes them an anchor for comparisons across papers.
blocks.zh: 准确性本身也容易被扭曲:同一个基准在修改后的法官即时或法官模型下可以产生非常不同的数字,彭菲尔德实验室(Penfield Labs)[17]显示一个被评价的法官配置接受了约63%的故意不正确,主题相关的答案. 成本和延迟更难悄悄地改善,这使得它们成为对各种文件进行比较的基础。

blocks.en: 2.3 Validity
blocks.zh: 2.3 有效性

blocks.en: An independent audit of LoCoMo [ 17 ] reported incorrect answers for 99 of 1,540 non-adversarial questions (6.4%). Other popular benchmarks contain similar issues. LongMemEval contains ground-truth arithmetic errors and mislabeled evidence, surfaced as GitHub issues by the community [ 12 ] .
blocks.zh: 对LoCoMo [17]的独立审计报告说,在1 540个非对抗性问题中,99个问题的答复不正确(6.4%)。 其他受欢迎的基准也有类似问题。 LongMemEval 包含了地面真实的算术错误和错误的标签证据,被社区称为GitHub问题[12].

blocks.en: Careful pipeline construction reduces error rates but does not eliminate them, so BEAM [ 24 ] adds human review, checking that every question is answerable. However, a test can pass that review and still be solvable without any memory, and then every system gets it right whether its memory works or not. Every DolphinBench test therefore has to fail without the relevant sessions as well as pass with them. We verify both automatically before a test ships, as described in the Test Construction section.
blocks.zh: 细心的管道建造降低了误差率但并没有消除误差率,因此BEAM [24] 增加了人文审查,检查每个问题都有答案. 然而,一个测试可以通过这个审查,并且仍然可以溶解而没有任何内存,然后每个系统都得到它的内存是否起作用. 因此,每一次海豚奔驰测试都必须在没有相关会话的情况下失败,并与它们一起通过. 如试验建造部分所述,我们自动在试验船前验证两者。

blocks.en: 3 DolphinBench
blocks.zh: 3只海豚奔驰

blocks.en: DolphinBench is a benchmark built to evaluate agents on their memory which directly tests task success. The benchmark covers three personas: Morgan, a startup CEO; Alex, an infrastructure engineer; and Riley, a product manager. These were chosen to have a wide coverage of different tools/apps the agent would use, queries across different task types, and thus different memory access patterns as well.
blocks.zh: Dolphin Bench是用来评估内存上的特效的基准,直接测试任务的成功. 基准包括三个人:刚起步的CEO摩根;基础设施工程师Alex;产品经理Riley。 选择这些工具是为了广泛涵盖代理人将使用的不同工具/应用程序、不同任务类型的查询,从而也涵盖不同的内存访问模式。

blocks.en: Each persona has a simulated history spanning several years, with 3,400--5,128 user messages totalling approximately 500k tokens 1 1 1 Measured with tiktoken’s o200k_base , over user-message content only. . The agents go through this simulated history, after which they are tested on tasks that require information from within those simulated sessions. The benchmark contains 600 tests, 200 per persona. Tool calls and apps (Notion, Gmail, GitHub, etc.) are both simulated to reproducibly test real world actions [ 28 , 31 ] .
blocks.zh: 每个人物都有一个模拟历史, 历时数年, 特工们经历这个模拟历史,然后对他们进行测试,以完成需要从模拟会议中获得信息的任务。 基准包括600项测试,每人200项。 工具调用和apps(Notion,Gmail,GitHub等)都进行了模拟,以复制测试真实世界的动作[28,31].

blocks.en: Morgan test 001: History. In a January session, Morgan mentions a coffee preference: “still doing blue bottle if i’m out early enough.” Instruction. “I’m out early. Please order one small latte for pickup.” Answer & grading. The agent must use place_order to order from Blue Bottle. A deterministic check requires the order to succeed, and an LLM judge checks that the restaurant is Blue Bottle.
blocks.zh: 摩根测试001:历史. 摩根在1月份的一次会议上提到了一种咖啡偏好:“如果我早点出来, 训导. 「我出院很早, 请点一杯小拿铁来取。” 回答分级( R) 。 代理商必须使用位置_ 顺序从蓝瓶订购 。 确定性检查需要命令才能成功,LLM法官检查餐厅是否是蓝瓶.

blocks.en: The request specifies the drink, size, and pickup, but not the cafe. The agent must use Morgan’s earlier preference to choose where to place the order.
blocks.zh: 请求中指定了饮料,大小,和皮卡,但不是咖啡馆. 代理商必须使用Morgan先前的偏好来选择将订单放在哪里.

blocks.en: 3.1 Construction
blocks.zh: 3.1 建筑业

blocks.en: Figure 1: The DolphinBench construction pipeline.
blocks.zh: 图1:海豚奔驰建造管道.

blocks.en: DolphinBench is built in hierarchical stages (Figure 1 ), an approach also used by BEAM [ 24 ] . We first outline each persona’s history over several years, then develop it into quarterly plans, weekly events, and conversations. The resulting messages and app records provide the basis for test construction.
blocks.zh: Dolphin Bench是分级建造的(图1),BEAM也采用了这种方法[24]. 我们首先概括了每个人在几年中的历史,然后将其发展成季度计划、每周活动和对话。 由此产生的信息和应用记录为测试构建提供了基础.

blocks.en: Personas
blocks.zh: 个人

blocks.en: We define each persona’s name, role, relationships, and tools, including calendar, email, CRM, and deployment tools. An LLM drafts these descriptions, which later stages use when planning events and writing messages. We update the definitions as people or tools change throughout the history. DolphinBench’s three personas are Morgan, a startup CEO who manages investors, hiring, board communication, and strategy; Alex, an infrastructure engineer who handles deploys, incidents, on-call rotations, and runbooks; and Riley, a product manager who runs experiments, funnels, and retention work.
blocks.zh: 我们定义每个人的姓名、角色、关系和工具,包括日历、电子邮件、客户关系管理和部署工具。 LLM起草这些描述,后期在规划事件和写信息时使用. 随着人或工具在整个历史中的变化,我们不断更新定义。 Dolphin Bench的三位人物是Morgan, 管理投资人、雇佣、董事会通讯和策略的创始首席执行官;Alex, 处理部署、事故、待命轮换和运行簿的基础设施工程师; Riley, 负责实验、漏斗和留存工作的产品经理。

blocks.en: History Planning
blocks.zh: 历史规划

blocks.en: We outline the persona’s work and personal life over several years. An LLM develops this narrative into quarterly plans, specifying dated events and the facts they are intended to establish or change. These include decisions, preferences, and developments in ongoing projects and relationships. We review the plans before generating the corresponding history.
blocks.zh: 我们概述了个人几年的工作和个人生活。 LLM将这一叙述发展为季度计划,具体说明日期事件及其旨在确定或改变的事实。 其中包括决定、偏好和进行中的项目和关系的发展。 我们在创造相应历史之前先审查这些计划。

blocks.en: An LLM then develops each quarter into weekly events and conversations. For each planned conversation, it specifies a date, why the persona contacts the agent, and what they ask for or share. The plan includes everyday exchanges alongside the quarter’s main events.
blocks.zh: 然后每个季度将LLM发展为每周的活动和对话。 对于每一个计划的对话,它都规定一个日期,为什么人与代理人联系,以及他们要求或分享什么. 计划包括日常交流,

blocks.en: History Generation
blocks.zh: 历史生成

blocks.en: Before writing these conversations, we update the simulated apps to reflect the planned events. An LLM specifies the required tool calls and arguments, such as updating an event in Google Calendar. We execute these calls in chronological order so that the messages can refer to the resulting app records.
blocks.zh: 在写这些对话之前,我们更新模拟应用以反映计划的事件. LLM指定了所需的工具调用和参数,例如更新Google日历中的事件. 我们按时间顺序执行这些调用,以便消息可以参考由此产生的应用记录.

blocks.en: The model writing the messages receives these records and tool outputs, together with the weekly plan, relevant facts, and earlier messages. It writes the user messages in the persona’s voice, using this context to keep them consistent with the apps and preceding conversations. Each released history ends at the first complete session that brings it to at least 500k user-message tokens.
blocks.zh: 撰写消息的模型会接收这些记录和工具输出,以及每周的计划,相关事实,以及更早的信息. 使用此语境, 使其与应用程序及之前的对话保持一致。 每个已发布的历史在第一个完整会话中结束,使其达到至少500k用户消息符号.

blocks.en: We author only the user side of each conversation, because each agent would reply differently. The agent produces its own replies during ingestion. QA benchmarks instead provide a fixed transcript of both sides [ 14 , 27 ] , which fits a system that reads a conversation but not one that participates in it.
blocks.zh: 我们只写每个对话的用户方,因为每个代理人会做出不同的答复. 该剂在摄入过程中产生自己的回复. 相反,质量保证基准提供了双方的固定记录 [14, 27] ,它符合一个阅读对话但不能参与对话的系统。

blocks.en: We record which facts each message mentions and which it introduces or changes. Before using a fact to construct a test, we check its description against the source messages and correct any claims they do not support.
blocks.zh: 我们记录每条信息提到哪些事实,其中提出哪些事实或作出哪些改变。 在使用一个事实来构建一个测试之前,我们对照源信息检查其描述,并纠正任何它们不支持的说法.

blocks.en: Test Construction
blocks.zh: 测试构造

blocks.en: An LLM proposes tasks that require the agent to use earlier information to complete new work. To design these tasks, it receives facts from the history, descriptions of the available tools, the evaluation date, and summaries of previously proposed tasks. For each task, it specifies the required facts, the intended actions, and what would be missing or wrong without the history. Each selected fact must affect a necessary part of the completed work.
blocks.zh: 一个LLM建议的任务要求代理人使用早期的信息来完成新的工作. 为了设计这些任务,它从历史、现有工具的描述、评价日期和以前提议的任务摘要中获取事实。 对于每一项任务,它都具体说明了所需的事实、打算采取的行动,以及没有历史将缺失或错失什么。 每个选定的事实必须影响到已完成工作的必要部分。

blocks.en: An LLM then receives the proposed task, relevant source messages and later updates, available tools, and app records. It writes the user request and grading checks. The request supplies the information needed to act while leaving the remembered details for the agent to determine. We avoid cues that announce a stored preference, such as “the way I usually do it”. Checks on remembered information cite the supporting source messages and require only the details needed for the task.
blocks.zh: 然后,一个LLM接收拟议任务、相关的源消息和以后的更新、可用的工具以及应用记录。 它会写用户请求和分级检查. 请求提供了采取行动所需的信息,同时将记忆中的细节留给代理人确定。 我们避免发出“我通常这样做的方式”这样的提示。 对已记住的信息的检查引用了支持源消息,只需要任务所需的细节.

blocks.en: We select the app records needed to carry out the task and add present-day records where the proposed situation requires them. These records supply ordinary task inputs without revealing the remembered answer. We review the request, app records, and grading checks against the source messages before verification.
blocks.zh: 我们选择执行任务所需的应用记录,并在拟议情况需要时添加现今记录。 这些记录提供普通的任务输入,而不透露被记住的答案. 我们先审查请求,应用记录,然后核对来源信息。

blocks.en: Test Verification
blocks.zh: 测试验证

blocks.en: For each test, we provide the original history messages needed to complete it as oracle messages. We run the test twice with GPT-5.6-Luna given these oracle messages, and twice without them (Figure 2 ). The task, tools, and starting app records remain the same. Both runs with history must pass every grading check, and both runs without history must fail.
blocks.zh: 对于每个测试,我们提供原始的历史信息 完成它作为先知信息。 我们用GPT-5.6-Luna进行了两次测试,给出了这些甲骨文信息,两次没有这些信息(图2)。 任务、工具和开始应用记录保持不变。 有历史记录的运行必须经过每一次分级检查,没有历史记录的运行必须失败.

blocks.en: We inspect the runs to check that failure without history reflects missing information rather than tool errors or defects in the test. We revise candidates that fail these checks and exclude those that do not meet the acceptance conditions.
blocks.zh: 我们检查运行以检查没有历史记录的失败是否反映了测试中缺少的信息而不是工具错误或缺陷. 我们修改那些没有通过这些检查的候选人,排除那些不符合接受条件的候选人。

blocks.en: Figure 2: Test verification. The agent must pass both runs with oracle messages and fail both runs without them.
blocks.zh: 图2:测试核实。 代理必须同时通过带有甲骨文消息的运行和没有它们同时失败的运行.

blocks.en: Table 2: Results on DolphinBench: comparing the accuracy, cost, and latency of agents using different memory systems across 600 tasks spanning three personas.
blocks.zh: 表2:海豚奔驰的结果:比较使用不同内存系统的代理的准确性,成本和耐久性,涉及跨越三人的600项任务.

blocks.en: 3.2 Grading & Metrics
blocks.zh: 3.2 分级和计量

blocks.en: We grade task completion by checking the agent’s tool calls against the actions and results required by the task. During test construction, we choose how to check each requirement: • We use an LLM judge [ 29 ] (GPT-5.6-Sol) when checking a requirement requires interpreting meaning, such as whether an email conveys a particular decision. The judge receives the user’s request and the arguments of the tool call being checked, and is instructed to accept equivalent wording. • We use deterministic checks when a requirement can be tested directly, such as whether a required tool was called or whether an identifier, number, date, or list matches the required value.
blocks.zh: 我们通过对照任务要求的行动和结果检查代理人的工具来评定任务的完成。 在试验建造期间,我们选择如何检查每项要求: 我们使用LLM法官[29](GPT-5.6-Sol)来检查一项要求需要解释含义时,例如电子邮件是否传达某一特定决定. 法官收到用户的要求和正在检查的工具呼叫的论据,并奉命接受同等措辞。 当一项要求可以直接测试时,我们使用确定性检查,例如要求的工具是否被调用,或者一个标识符、数字、日期或清单是否与要求的数值相符。

blocks.en: We use an LLM judge [ 29 ] (GPT-5.6-Sol) when checking a requirement requires interpreting meaning, such as whether an email conveys a particular decision. The judge receives the user’s request and the arguments of the tool call being checked, and is instructed to accept equivalent wording.
blocks.zh: 我们使用LLM法官[29](GPT-5.6-Sol)来检查一项要求需要解释含义时,例如电子邮件是否传达某一特定决定. 法官收到用户的请求和正在检查的工具呼叫的论据,并奉命接受同等措辞。

blocks.en: We use deterministic checks when a requirement can be tested directly, such as whether a required tool was called or whether an identifier, number, date, or list matches the required value.
blocks.zh: 当一项要求可以直接测试时,我们使用确定性检查,例如要求的工具是否被调用,或者一个标识符、数字、日期或清单是否与要求的数值相符。

blocks.en: The checks must establish that each required action was completed correctly. For example, an email must have both the correct recipient and the required content in the same send call; satisfying those checks across different emails does not count. If a task requires two separate emails, one send call cannot count as both. A task passes only when every check passes.
blocks.zh: 检查必须确定每项所需行动完成得正确。 例如,电子邮件必须同时有正确的接收者和同一发送呼叫中所要求的内容;满足不同电子邮件的检查不计数。 如果任务需要两个单独的电子邮件,一个发送呼叫不能算作两者兼有. 只有在每次检查都通过时,任务才会通过。

blocks.en: Every submission must report accuracy, total cost across ingestion and testing, and median task latency. We calculate accuracy as the fraction of tasks passed and take the median of the individual test latencies across all personas.
blocks.zh: 每次提交都必须报告准确性、摄入和测试的总成本以及中位数任务延迟。 我们计算准确度,因为所通过任务的一小部分,并采用个人测试延迟的中位数。

blocks.en: 4 Results
blocks.zh: 4 结果

blocks.en: We evaluate agents with different combinations of harnesses, language models, and memory systems. Table 2 reports the accuracy, cost, and latency of each combination.
blocks.zh: 我们用不同组合的绳子、语言模型和记忆系统来评价代理人。 表2报告每种组合的准确性、成本和耐久性。

blocks.en: Accuracy is the percentage of tasks passed. Total cost covers ingestion and testing, including memory processing. Latency is the median time per test, including tool use.
blocks.zh: 准确性是指通过的任务的百分比. 总成本包括摄入和测试,包括内存处理. 延迟是每次测试的中位时间,包括工具的使用.

blocks.en: Memory performance reflects the capabilities of the model, the harness, and the memory system working together. With Hermes [ 15 ] and Mem0 [ 4 ] , accuracy reaches 70.67% with GPT-5.6-Luna, compared with 47.83% with MiniMax M3. The memory systems also rank differently across configurations: Mem0 scores highest with both Hermes models, while Honcho [ 18 ] scores highest with Claude Code [ 2 ] and Claude Sonnet 5.
blocks.zh: 内存性能反映了模型,牵引,和内存系统协同工作的能力. 与Hermes [15]和Mem0 [4] 相比,GPT-5.6-Luna的精度达到了70.67%,而MiniMax M3.的精度达到了47.83%. 内存系统在配置上也排名不同: Mem0的得分最高的是两个赫尔梅斯模型,而翁乔[18]的得分最高的是克劳德代号[2]和克劳德·索内5.

blocks.en: Higher accuracy need not require longer response times. With Hermes and GPT-5.6-Luna, Mem0 improves accuracy over built-in memory by five percentage points and reduces median task latency from 44.35 to 37.69 seconds, while total cost rises from $61.48 to $96.21.
blocks.zh: 提高准确性不需要较长的反应时间。 与赫尔墨斯和GPT-5.6-卢纳, Mem0比内置内存提高了5个百分点的精度,并将任务间歇的中位数从44.35秒降至37.69秒,而总成本则从61.48美元增至96.2美元.

blocks.en: Lower cost and higher accuracy can also come with longer response times. With the same harness and model, Hindsight [ 9 ] costs $84.65 compared with Honcho’s $142.85 and scores one percentage point higher, but its median task latency is 55.31 seconds compared with Honcho’s 44.66 seconds.
blocks.zh: 成本降低和准确性提高也可能带来较长的反应时间。 Hindsight[9]与Honcho的142.85相比,

blocks.en: Evaluating each configuration on all three metrics lets DolphinBench map the Pareto frontier and helps users choose the configuration that best matches their accuracy, cost, and latency requirements.
blocks.zh: 在所有三个度量器上对每个配置进行评价,让Dolphin Bench绘制Pareto前沿图,并帮助用户选择最适合其准确性,成本和耐久性要求的配置.

blocks.en: We release the configuration, cost calculations, and full trace of every run in Table 2 (tool calls, arguments, and per-check verdicts) alongside the dataset.
blocks.zh: 我们公布表2中的配置、成本计算和所有运行(工具呼叫、参数和每个检查结果)以及数据集。

blocks.en: 5 Limitations
blocks.zh: 5 限制

blocks.en: We generate conversation histories rather than collect them from real users. These histories may not capture the variety of writing styles, languages, and interaction patterns found in real conversations. Checking facts against source messages and verifying the tests helps catch errors, but inconsistencies may remain.
blocks.zh: 我们创造对话历史,而不是从真正的用户那里收集。 这些历史可能无法捕捉真实对话中发现的写作风格、语言和互动模式的多样性。 对照源信息检查事实和核实测试有助于捕捉错误,但不一致之处可能依然存在.

blocks.en: Three personas cover only a small part of knowledge work. They exercise different tools and memory requirements, but do not represent domains such as law, medicine, or long-term customer support. The construction pipeline supports adding personas to broaden this coverage.
blocks.zh: 三人只负责一小部分知识工作。 它们行使不同的工具和内存要求,但并不代表法律,医学,或长期客户支持等领域. 建造管道支持增加人员以扩大这一覆盖范围。

blocks.en: Agents interact with simulated apps rather than live services. The apps support selected operations and errors, but do not reproduce the full behavior of production systems, including service outages and changes made by other users during a task. This makes the tasks reproducible while leaving some difficulties of real deployments untested.
blocks.zh: 代理商与模拟应用程序而不是现场服务交互. 应用程序支持选定的操作和错误,但不复制生产系统的全部行为,包括服务中断和任务期间其他用户所做的更改. 这使得任务可以复制,同时留下一些实际部署的困难而没有经过测试。

blocks.en: Each task requires one to four separately graded actions, though agents may make additional calls to find information or correct mistakes. These tasks test whether agents use remembered information correctly without requiring long workflows. Longer tasks would extend the evaluation to using memory across many dependent steps.
blocks.zh: 每项任务需要一至四个单独分级的行动,不过特工人员可能会发出额外的呼叫来寻找信息或纠正错误. 这些任务检验代理是否正确使用记忆中的信息而不需要较长的工作流程. 较长的任务将扩大评价范围,将内存用于许多不同步骤。

blocks.en: Agents process the full history before taking any tests. This lets us compare agents against the same completed history, but does not test how they handle new conversations and tasks arriving throughout an ongoing evaluation. Interleaving ingestion and testing would better represent that continuous use.
blocks.zh: 特工们在接受任何测试之前 都要处理全部历史 这让我们可以将代理人与同样的已完成的历史进行比较,但并不检验他们如何处理在整个持续评估过程中到达的新的对话和任务。 中断摄入和测试将更好地代表这种持续使用。

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: DolphinBench evaluates agent memory through the actions agents take. We grade task completion, verify every test through agent runs with and without the relevant history, and require every result to report cost and latency alongside accuracy.
blocks.zh: Dolphin Bench通过特工采取的行动来评价代理记忆. 我们分级任务完成,通过毒剂核查每一次测试是否具有相关历史,并要求每个结果同时报告成本和耐久性以及准确性。

blocks.en: Our results show that a more accurate agent need not be slower, and a more expensive agent need not be more accurate. We therefore compare accuracy, cost, and latency together to assess each agent configuration as a whole.
blocks.zh: 我们的结果显示,更准确的剂剂不需要慢一点,更昂贵的剂剂不需要更准确. 因此,我们共同比较准确性、成本和耐久性,以评估每个代理配置的整体情况。

blocks.en: We intend to keep the benchmark growing: histories that exceed model context windows, more personas, longer tasks, and interleaved ingestion and testing that better matches real deployments. As agents improve, the benchmarks should become harder with them.
blocks.zh: 我们打算保持基准不断增长:超越模式上下文窗口的历史、更多的人、更长的任务、以及更符合实际部署的互换摄入和测试。 随着代理人的改进,基准应该随着他们的提高而变得更加困难。
